tier_reason: Upgraded from C to A. The README Benchmark section gives cycles per 64-bit value (Sirius64 5.007 vs xoshiro256++ 6.331, xoshiro256** 6.158, pcg64 DXSM 8.623, RXS-M-XS 6.870, romutrio 5.842) on an Intel Core Ultra 7 265H with gcc 13.3.0. The benchmark code tools/benchmark.c is public and states its compile line (-O3 -march=native -mtune=native). lemire/testingRNG independently corroborates the result: sirius64 at 4.29 vs pcg64 at 2.53 and mersennetwister at 1.68 on a Xeon Gold 6548N with GCC 14.

corrections.hardware: Intel Core Ultra 7 265H (16 CPUs), Ubuntu 24.04 under WSL2; independent run in lemire/testingRNG on a Xeon Gold 6548N
corrections.claimed_speedup: 5.007 cycles per 64-bit value vs xoshiro256++ 6.331, xoshiro256** 6.158, xoroshiro128++ 6.295, romutrio 5.842, pcg64 RXS-M-XS 6.870, pcg64 DXSM 8.623 (splitmix64 4.985); relative speed 99.6% of splitmix64 vs 78.7%/81.0%/72.6%/57.8%
corrections.caveats: Very new single-author design; its statistical quality (PractRand, TestU01, SmokeRand) is self-reported. Timed with rdtscp under WSL2; the author notes rankings changed on other machines. lemire/testingRNG independently lists sirius64 at 4.29 vs pcg64 2.53 and mersennetwister 1.68 (GCC 14, Xeon Gold 6548N). It is only about 1.25x faster than xoshiro256++ and ties splitmix64.

notes: The tier was upgraded because the benchmark source, compiler, flags and CPU model are all public. The baselines are other PRNGs, not std::mt19937 directly. It has 2 stars and its last commit was on 2026-09-29.

tier_reason: The README shows Catch2 benchmark output (UnitTest/Benchmark.cpp) for 1M values. The Blackman/Vigna C reference took 1.09 ms and AVX next4() with no sum took 526 us. The hardware is a Ryzen 7 1700 VM, but the compiler and flags are not stated, so the tier is C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Reference C xoshiro256+ 1.09 ms per 1M values vs AVX2 next4() 526 us (about 2.07x, derived from page data); serial next4() 1.93 ms vs AVX2 next4() 526 us (about 3.7x, derived from page data)
corrections.caveats: Rounded numbers; compiler and flags unstated; measured in a 2-core VM. The author says the gain disappears if the four-wide values are extracted and used one by one. Compared only against the scalar reference, not std::mt19937. Last commit 2021-08-21 (over 3 years ago).

notes: The last commit was on 2021-08-21, more than 5 years ago, so maintenance_status was corrected to abandoned. It has 14 stars and an MIT license, both confirmed.
